source: (INVESTIGATIVE) [Observe the geezers to identify their leader.]
Here, fellas. Have some birdseed, on the house.
Mind if I take a picture of you?
How come you're hanging out in the street?
You guys know anything about that clock over there?
Alright, I'll leave you to it.
Honk honk honk. HONK HONK. Honk HONK
Fine. I'll be back when I have more witnesses.
(INVESTIGATIVE) ...What's that you're sitting around on, there?
Come on, geezers. The hand. Cough it up.
Would you look at that - a steam clock hand. I'll be taking that, if you don't mind.
Now don't let it happen again, alright? I got my eyes on you.
HONK. HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK.
I guess that's as reasonable an explanation as I expected.
Not what I wanted to hear.
So where is it? Am I going to have to get a new one?
...The mechanic? I guess I could try.
Well, this has been a delightful conversation. Have a good day.
HONK. HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK HONK. Honk?
Well, this has been a delightful conversation. Have a good day.
Well, this has been a delightful conversation. Have a good day.
[The geezers swarm the handful of birdseed, picking away at it. You've served your purpose - now, they only feel the need for seed.]
[The geezers look amongst themselves, and then towards a particularly large member of their posse. The big geezer scoffs, looking back at the clock and then back at you with a mischievous grin.]
[The large geezer shakes its head, honks one last time, and returns to picking at food in the snowy gutter. Geezers don't snitch, it seems.]
I'll get to the bottom of this, geezers.
Well, this has been a delightful conversation. Have a good day.
[The heads of the geezers shoot up in surprise, but soon enough return to their waddling and gutterpicking. They're too spread out for a good picture, anyway.]
[Appeal to the eldest geezer] Excuse me, sir?
Here, you geezers. If I give you this birdseed, will you all group up nicely?
Would you all mind grouping up a bit?
[The geezers mostly ingore your request, and remain too spread out to nicely capture in a picture.]
Here, you geezers. If I give you this birdseed, will you all group up nicely?
Would you all mind grouping up a bit?
[You throw some birdseed on the ground, and the geezers gleefully pounce the seedy treats. Now's your chance.]
[Let them enjoy the birdseed in peace]
[They make a point to ignore you as loudly as possible. You'll need to bribe them.]
Stay right here. I'll be right back, alright?
Fine, fine. What else is new?
Not the most original shot, but it'll do.
[The geezers congratulate each other on being so photogenic.]
[The geezers go silent, staring you down past offended beaks.]

[Continuous observation reveals what appears to be some notion of gerontocratic rule - the eldest of the geezers, a large, greying one, appears to be treated with more respect than the others. All geese are equals, it seems, but some more than others.]
I'll bear that in mind. Might be useful information.
[The geezers regard you with suspicion, but soon return to their scheduled gutterpicking.]
Ahem. I wanted to ask you geezers something.
[The eldest geezer pauses, lifting its head and regarding you carefully for a moment. It nods regally, as if allowing you to speak.]
Would your highness be interested in having his portrait taken?

[The gerontocratic geezer gestures gently, as if having considered and approved your request. It lets out a noble honk, amassing the other geezers around it. Looking at it, it would make a very nice group picture.]
...Actually, nevermind. Down with the ruling class.
[The geezers look back at a still goose lying amongst them - it would be macabre, but upon closer inspection you notice it's just a geezer plushie. A child's toy.]
[The geezers honk and shuffle away as you pocket the paltry but provably poultry plushie.]
That's all. See you all later.
Honk-honk. Honk, honk honk HONK HONK honk. HONK-honk?
You gotta honk about it. HOnk.
What's honk got to do with it?
I was told you might know something about it. Might even have done something to it.
Jigs up, fellas. I know you tore the hand from old Grandfather Steam.
You know, some people don't like you geezers much.
I'm just saying, it has to be cold.
One of you isn't moving. Is he okay?
[The geezers seem mostly to regard each other as equals, bumping, honking and shoving against each other whenever deemed appropriate to do so.]
Surely they have a leader, though?
